doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: King Oliver's Chicago clubs and the Lincoln Gardens
summary: Barker never heard Oliver's band in Chicago but later played at the Lincoln Gardens on a New Orleans excursion, noting David Jones and Armstrong's coolness.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So you go to see King Oliver. Did you hear . . . you heard his band?
I never heard King Oliver’s band in Chicago. They show you a picture where he played in a ball park. You seen that picture in one of them books?
As far as me going to the club, I didn’t go. It was Savoy and Royal Gardens. The Royal Gardens is something else. What they call it now? Not the Savoy. It was the Royal Gardens.
No. That’s something else. There was a white club. There was . . . I almost had it. It wasn’t the Savoy. It was the Royal Gardens, and what’s another club? It was the same club, changed their name.

That’s one and the same. The Savoy and the Lincoln. I played there when we went to Chicago on the excursion. We played there. I told you David Jones just waved at Louis. Never come and hugged like two long lost brothers. And Louis always held that in to him, I guess. Their old grudges. Last time I seen David Jones, I working at Lee Collins’s band. Never made no money with that band. All we did was flop. Nobody came out, because Lee Collins had competition there. Papa Celestin was out there. Chris Kelly was out there. Kid Rena was out there. Buddy Petit was in and out of town. [? (inaudible)] he’s away, over there in Bogalousa somewhere, shacking up with some woman. He leave his wife here without no food, and she’s gonna send something, but he don’t send nothing. He go out and stay five, six weeks and come back and expect to get big welcome, but he ain’t coming home with no money.
